estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Textual embedding analysis of similarity among the creative products. The embedding model, exact similarity metric, comparison pool, aggregation, and statistical model are not stated. The main text reports only that similarity did not significantly increase with AI.

sources.locator: PDF p. 21, Experiment 1, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis
sources.quote: we employed textual analysis techniques (embedding) to assess the similarity of the creative products.

sources.locator: PDF p. 21, Experiment 1, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis
sources.quote: Interestingly, our findings showed no significant increase in similarity among AI-assisted outputs compared to those created independently, indicating that AI use in our study did not homogenize creative work.

estimates.notes: Retained as a qualitative full-sample AI-versus-no-AI contrast. No arm means, SDs, SEs, numerical difference, coefficient, test statistic, p-value, confidence interval, or similarity-analysis count is printed. The general study count is not substituted for an unstated analysis-specific denominator. Empty source fields lists accompany qualitative evidence only. The task asks each person to produce a flash fiction, consistent with the reconciled S1-O4 diversity classification, but the exact comparison and aggregation remain unknown. The model specification for this supplementary analysis is not reported, so the post-treatment adjustment documented for the separate creativity regressions is not assumed here. Online Appendix D is cited for further supplementary details on PDF p. 22 but was unavailable. No numerical result is inferred from the statement about significance.

open_items: Obtain unadjusted AI-versus-no-AI contrasts or models omitting post-treatment covariates for all human-rated creativity outcomes. The main-text regression tables all include rater AI identification. Arm-specific means, participant-level SDs, and arm analysis counts are not printed; full-sample descriptives cannot substitute for them (PDF pp. 19, 26, 40-47).

Exact randomized totals, arm sizes, and attrition by arm remain unreported. Experiment 1 gives a participation/final sample count, not a separately labeled randomized count (PDF p. 16). Experiment 2 distinguishes registration/IQ-test, information, submission, and selected analysis stages (PDF pp. 23-24). The subgroup sizes in AI-interaction analyses do not explicitly identify full-arm totals and were not added to create counts (PDF pp. 21, 28).

For S1-O4, obtain both arm levels, the embedding model and metric, the compared-output pool, aggregation and analysis units, the analysis-specific person count, model covariates, and numerical uncertainty. The saved PDF reports only a qualitative significance conclusion (PDF p. 21).

For S2-O7, establish whether the similarity analysis compares different people and how multiple submissions from one participant are handled. Obtain participant-linked comparison definitions, model covariates, analysis counts, arm levels, SDs/SEs, and intervals before assigning the diversity/across_people classification (PDF pp. 24, 28-29; final.open_items in the screening form).

Participant dependence in Experiment 2 needs resolution: the regressions use works as observations and report robust SEs, with no stated clustering by participant. Some people supplied multiple works (PDF p. 24; Tables 4-8, PDF pp. 43-47).

The online appendices and posted analysis output remain unavailable. On 2026-10-10, Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the printed OSF project URL, its file-list API, and the related registration API each failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No supplement contents or posted data were inferred from these failures.

Confirm whether the related preregistration at https://osf.io/g49yd/ applies to the realized experiments and identifies a primary outcome. The local forms/data/c366.json audit describes planned AI-tool, AI-collaborator, and no-AI conditions, whereas this PDF reports AI and no-AI conditions. The manuscript makes no preregistration statement and the protocol could not be independently accessed in this session.
Experiment 2 recruitment country is not explicitly stated (PDF pp. 22-24). Chinese currency and the manuscript discussion do not establish all recruitment locations.
Cross-experiment participant overlap and overlap with other papers remain unstated. PDF p. 16, footnote 1 identifies a broader research project but no particular shared-sample paper.
The paper names GPT-4 but does not print a model release year or API snapshot; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 16).
notes: Extraction checked on 2026-10-10. Read the entire markdown conversion in contiguous chunks through its final figure captions, including references and all tables. Inspected all PDF tables and figures and checked cited page text with PyMuPDF. PDF page indices plus one agree with printed page numbers. Statistical inventory: Tables 1 and 3 contain full-sample outcome means, SDs, and correlations; Table 2 contains the Experiment 1 main and interaction regressions; Tables 4-5 contain Experiment 2 main regressions; Tables 6-8 contain its interaction regressions. The regression tables report robust SEs, observations, and model fit. Results sections give additional exact p-values and conditional-slope tests, and Figures 4-8 show moderation results. The supplementary sections give similarity results, AI-interaction subgroup comparisons, and subjective perceptions. All human-rated treatment regressions are excluded because their rater AI-identification covariate is measured after output creation. The definition is explicit on PDF p. 19: "we controlled for the AI identification ratio, calculated as the proportion of raters who believed AI was used in creating each story." Tables 1 and 3 provide no arm-specific descriptives or unadjusted treatment effects. The retained story-similarity record has no numerical effect or precision; the lyric-similarity classification remains unresolved as recorded in the final screening form. The study sample counts refer to people; Experiment 2 work counts are not treated as people. The one-week lyric task involves AI availability during writing and is not an after-AI follow-up. The local PDF SHA-256 was checked against forms/citations/c366.json. No calculations, imputed arm sizes, or figure-coordinate estimates were used.
